source: Original (authored 2026-10-27, calculator, radians; parallel of 2-5PQ_Trig-statistics P3). Triangle ABC: AB = 6 cm, AC = 10 cm, angle BAC = 1.1 rad. Moved to problem 1 on 2026-10-28.

parts.label: a
parts.description: AB = 6, AC = 10, angle BAC = 1.1 rad. Find BC.
parts.tolerance: Accept 9.03 or the display with an ellipsis. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0. Degree-mode value 4.00 earns the final A0.
parts.notes: M1 for using the cosine rule. A1 for the correct substitution 6^2 + 10^2 - 2(6)(10) cos 1.1. A1 for 9.03 (radian mode).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the area of triangle ABC.
parts.tolerance: Accept 26.7 or the display with an ellipsis. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0. Degree-mode value 0.576 earns A0.

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate. The answer must be in radians: 36.3 degrees earns the final A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for using the sine rule (or cosine rule). A1 for pairing AB = 6 with angle ACB. A1 for 0.634. Wrong method: pairing 10 with angle ACB gives 1.41, which is angle ABC: M1A0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's BC in (a).

source: Original (authored 2026-10-27, calculator; parallel of 2-5PQ_Trig-statistics P4). Plot ABC: AB = 40 m, angle A = 68 deg, angle B = 47 deg; second plot sides 24 m and 35 m, area 320 m^2, obtuse included angle. Moved to problem 2 on 2026-10-28.

parts.label: a
parts.description: AB = 40, angle BAC = 68, angle ABC = 47. Write down angle ACB.
parts.notes: A1 for 65. 'Write down': no working needed.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept 32.3 or the display with an ellipsis. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for using the sine rule. A1 for pairing AC with 47 deg and 40 with angle ACB. A1 for 32.3. Wrong method: pairing AC with 68 deg gives 40.9, which is BC: M1A0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's angle in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the area of the plot.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate, including 599 from AC = 32.3. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for (1/2)ab sin C with two sides and the angle between them, e.g. (1/2)(40)(AC) sin 68. A1 for 599. Wrong method: (1/2)(40)(AC) sin 65 = 585: M0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's AC in (b).

parts.label: d
parts.description: Second plot: sides 24 and 35, area 320, included angle obtuse. Find the angle.
parts.tolerance: A1 for 130 (3 s.f.) or the display with an ellipsis (130.367...). 130.4 with no ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for (1/2)(24)(35) sin theta = 320. A1 (implied) for the acute value 49.6. A1 for the obtuse value 130. Giving only the acute value earns M1A1A0.

source: Original (added 2026-10-28 at Chris's request; replaces the two-boats problem). Unit circle: P(a, b) at pi/3, T(c, d) at 225 degrees, R(k, 0.6) and S on y = 0.6, alpha and beta the angles to OR and OS.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Unit circle: P(a, b) at angle pi/3. Write down the exact values of a and b.
parts.tolerance: Accept 0.5 for a. b must be exact: 0.866 earns A0.
parts.notes: A1 for a = 1/2, A1 for b = sqrt3/2, independently. Wrong method: swapping sine and cosine (a = sqrt3/2, b = 1/2): A0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write 225 degrees in radians as an exact multiple of pi.
parts.tolerance: Accept 225pi/180 or 1.25pi. 3.93 earns A0 (not a multiple of pi).
parts.notes: A1 for 5pi/4 or an equivalent exact multiple of pi.

parts.label: c
parts.description: T(c, d) at angle 225 degrees on the unit circle. Write down the exact values of c and d.
parts.notes: A1 for c = -sqrt2/2, A1 for d = -sqrt2/2, each with its sign; sqrt2/2 with no minus sign earns A0 for that value.

parts.label: d
parts.description: R(k, 0.6) lies on the unit circle in the first quadrant. Find k.
parts.notes: M1 for x^2 + y^2 = 1 with y = 0.6 (Pythagoras in the unit circle), or k = cos(arcsin 0.6). A1 for 0.8. Giving k = +-0.8 as the final answer earns M1A0 (the negative root belongs to S). Wrong method: k = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4: M0A0.

parts.label: e
parts.description: sin(theta) = 0.6 has two solutions alpha and beta for 0 <= theta <= 2pi (angles to OR and OS). Find alpha and beta.
parts.tolerance: Accept 0.644 and 2.50, or the displays with an ellipsis. Accept 2.50 from the rounded alpha = 0.644. Answers in degrees (36.9, 143) earn A0 for each value; the M1 can still be awarded. A value cut short without an ellipsis (0.6435) earns A0.
parts.notes: A1 for alpha = 0.644. M1 for beta = pi - alpha, or for the symmetry of S and R about the y-axis. A1 for beta = 2.50. Wrong methods: pi + alpha = 3.79 or 2pi - alpha = 5.64 (these have sin = -0.6): M0A0.

source: Original (authored 2026-10-27, calculator; parallel of 2-5PQ_Trig-statistics P1). Tree FT; A is 35 m from F, elevation 32 deg; B on [AF], 15 m from A. Moved to problem 4 on 2026-10-28.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Tree FT, A 35 m from F, elevation of T from A is 32 deg. Find the height.
parts.tolerance: Accept 21.9 or the display with an ellipsis. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for tan 32 = FT/35. A1 for 21.9. Wrong methods: 35 sin 32 = 18.5 or 35/tan 32 = 56.0 earn M0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for any valid method: 35/cos 32, Pythagoras with 35 and FT, or FT/sin 32. A1 for 41.3. Wrong method: 35/sin 32 = 66.0 earns M0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's height in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: B is on [AF], 15 m from A. Find the angle of elevation of T from B.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate, including 47.6 from FT = 21.9. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0.
parts.notes: A1 for BF = 20. M1 for tan theta = height / their BF. A1 for 47.6. Wrong method: using 15 as the horizontal distance gives 55.6: A0M1A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's height in (a).
